headline: NHRA approves Mohawk Tannery plan update, audit and insurance contracts, and FY2027 payment standards; tables operating budget then approves it after closed session.
summary: The Nashua Housing and Redevelopment Authority approved several resolutions, including updates to the Mohawk Tannery redevelopment plan, a two-year audit contract with EFPR Group for $74,950, insurance contracts with Housing Insurance Services totaling $286,347.87, FY2027 Section 8 payment standards, and a $75,478.39 tenant account receivables write-off. The board initially tabled the FY2027 operating budget, then approved it along with salary recommendations after a nonpublic session on personnel matters.
decisions: Approved Resolution No. 26-2509 reaffirming prior actions and recommending Mohawk Tannery redevelopment plan updates to the Board of Aldermen.
Approved Resolution No. 26-2510 awarding a two-year audit services contract to EFPR Group, CPAs, PLLC for $74,950.
Approved Resolution No. 26-2511 awarding insurance coverage contracts to Housing Insurance Services, Inc. totaling $275,016.73 plus $11,331.14.
Approved Resolution No. 26-2512 authorizing FY2027 Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher payment standards effective November 1, 2026.
Approved Resolution No. 26-2513 approving the Public Housing Tenant Account Receivables write-off for $75,478.39 and Nashua Park View Apartments, LLC write-off for $551.88.
Tabled Resolution No. 26-2514 approving the Operating Budget for Fiscal Year ending September 30, 2027.
Approved paying bills from the Cash Disbursement List (checks 73559-73778) and Park View Apartments Cash Disbursement List (checks 6077-6082), including ACH debits and investment accounts.
After rising from nonpublic session, approved Resolution No. 26-2514 and the salary recommendations.

plain_text:
MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING 
OF THE COMMISSIONERS OF THE 
NASHUA HOUSING AND REDEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY 
HELD ON SEPTEMBER 18, 2026 
 
 The Commissioners of the Nashua Housing and Redeve lopment Authority (NHRA) held 
its regular meeting at the office of the Nashua Housing and Redevelopment Authority, 40 East 
Pearl Street, Nashua, New Hampshire, at 8:30 a.m. o n Friday, September 18, 2026. 
Chairperson Eric Wilson called the meeting to order, and the Recording Secretary called the 
roll at approximately 8:32 a.m. with the following responses: 
   
Present Absent 
Eric Wilson  
Paul Deschenes  
Helen Honorow  
Thomas Monahan  
James Tollner  
 
 The following persons were also present: Bob Mack,  Director, City of Nashua Welfare 
Department; Tonia Knisley, Voices of Major Drive; B ob Keating, Granite State Organizing 
Project; Victoria Markiewicz, Granite State Organiz ing Project; Carolyn Murphy, Resident; 
Joseph Plodzik, Resident; William Tucker,  Wadleigh , Starr and Peters, PLLC,; Cary Soto-
Lozada, Finance Manager; Scott Costa, Assistant Exe cutive Director; Lynn Lombardi, 
Executive Director, and Deanna Brooks, Recording Secretary.  
 
MINUTES: 
 
 The Chairperson entertained a motion to waive the reading of the Authority’s regular 
meeting minutes dated August 21, 2026, accept them,  and place them on file. Mr. Tollner 
made a motion, and Mr. Monahan seconded the motion. The Chairperson asked if there were 
any comments, additions/deletions, corrections, or discussion. 
 
 There being no further discussion, the motion pass ed unanimously. 
 
COMMUNICATIONS: 
 
 The Chairperson entertained a motion to waive the reading of the Communications, accept 
them, and place them on file. Mr. Monahan made a mo tion to accept, and Ms. Honorow 
DRAFT
seconded the motion. The Communications were as follows:  Monthly Operational Reports – 
August 2026 – consisting of the Public Housing and Section 8 Waiting List and Applications 
Report; Work Order Report; Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher Program (HCVP) Utilization 
Report and Rent Collections Report. 
 
 The Chairperson asked if there were any comments o r discussion. 
 
 Mr. Deschenes inquired about the rent receivables and acknowledged improvements are 
being made but expressed concern and asked whether negotiations are underway.  Ms. 
Lombardi stated that this remains an ongoing focus,  noting that negotiations have occurred 
with residents who defaulted, and she is currently working with the attorney to file with the 
court.   
 
 Mr. Monahan stated that it is unfortunate there is  a resolution for the tenant account 
receivables write-off and noted an increase in non- payments from the previous month. He 
expressed concern that action is needed and acknowledged that the NHRA is making efforts 
to work with residents but emphasized that the situation requires attention. 
 
 Mr. Wilson noted concerns that the rent receivable s are very high and appear to be 
worsening rather than improving. 
 
  Ms. Honorow asked about the success of payments a t Knightsbridge and whether the high 
number of non-payments at Maynard Homes is related to the redevelopment project. Ms. 
Lombardi explained that Knightsbridge is leased dir ectly to Harbor Care, and therefore 
payments are made by the agency rather than individual residents. She said that non-payment 
of rent at Maynard Homes is not related to the redevelopment project. 
 
 Mr. Tollner questioned whether the write-off resol ution amounts were influenced by unit 
size or by non-payment over time. Ms. Lombardi explained that unit size does not affect the 
amount owed, as rent is based on thirty percent of household income, or in some cases, a flat 
rent amount. 
 
 Mr. Monahan reported that the current total number  of applicants on the waiting lists is 
4,332 for Public Housing, 5,420 for Section 8 HCV, 521 for Cotton Mill PBV, 370 for Salmon 
Brook, and 1,286 for Monahan Manor. He stated that the NHRA is doing a great job and noted 
that there was not a significant increase in the waitlists, but he remains attentive to the trend.  
 
DRAFT
Mr. Wilson commented that the economy may be contr ibuting to the impact and advised 
continued monitoring. 
 
 The Chairperson asked if there were any additional  comments or discussion. There being 
none, the motion passed unanimously.  
 
EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR’S REPORT: 
 
 At Maynard Homes, building 1 is underway with seco nd floor framing following completion 
of site water flow testing, with the steel beam pos itioned and coated in intumescent fire-
retardant paint; building 2 has completed footings and frost walls, with the elevator tower 
hoistway ongoing; and buildings 3 and 4 have completed their slabs and are ready for framing. 
 
 Funding applications for Phase 2 of the Maynard Ho mes Redevelopment were submitted 
to the New Hampshire Housing Finance Authority (NHHFA), Federal Home Loan Bank, and 
the City of Nashua’s Housing Revolving Fund. In support of the Phase 2 LIHTC application, 
three waiver requests were submitted to NHHFA for c onsideration by its Board. I’m very 
pleased to report that the NHHFA Board approved all  waivers at its September 16, 2026, 
Board meeting. 
 
 Boiler replacements at George F. Robinson Manor an d Whitney Street have been 
completed, and Highline Mechanical is now onsite at  Sullivan Terrace North to begin boiler 
replacements. 
 The NHRA and the City of Nashua will partner to ex pand access to energy-efficient electric 
heating and cooling technologies for low- and moder ate-income households. This 
collaborative initiative, involving the City of Nashua, Gradient, and Resilient Building Group, 
will provide fifty (50) renter-friendly window heat  pumps to households throughout the 
community. 
 Gradient Window Heat Pumps can be installed withou t permanent modifications to a 
property, making them an ideal option for renters who may be unable to install traditional heat 
pump systems. Gradient will supply the heat pumps, while Resilient Building Group will 
conduct in-home assessments to determine whether ea ch unit is appropriate for the 
household and provide technical assistance throughout the installation process. The City of 
Nashua will administer the grant, coordinate commun ity outreach, and oversee the overall 
program. 
DRAFT
The NHRA will begin identifying housing units that  are suitable for the window heat pump 
installations and will coordinate with program part ners to facilitate implementation. We are 
excited to partner with the City of Nashua, Gradien t, and Resilient Building Group on this 
innovative project and look forward to helping expand access to energy-efficient heating and 
cooling solutions for Nashua residents. 
 
 The Chairperson entertained a motion to approve th e Executive Director’s Report. Mr. 
Monahan made a motion, and Mr. Tollner seconded the  motion. The Chairperson asked if 
there were any comments or discussion. 
 
 Mr. Deschenes sought clarification on whether the heat pumps function similarly to air 
conditioners. Ms. Lombardi said that they provide both heating and cooling. 
 
 Mr. Monahan noted that the waivers approved by New  Hampshire Housing were 
unanimous. 
  
  There being no further discussion, the motion pas sed unanimously.  
 
NEW BUSINESS: 
 
RESOLUTION NO. 26-2509 
BY THE NASHUA HOUSING AND REDEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY  
REAFFIRMING THE ACTIONS TAKEN IN RESOLUTIONS NO. 24-2454,  
NO. 24-2456, AND NO. 25-2475, AND RECOMMENDING TO THE CITY OF NASHUA  
BOARD OF ALDERMEN THAT IT APPROVE UPDATES TO THE REDEVELOPMENT 
 PLAN FOR THE FORMER MOHAWK TANNERY SITE 
 
 The Chairperson entertained a motion to approve Resolution No. 26-2509. Mr. Monahan 
made a motion, and Mr. Deschenes seconded the motio n. The Chairperson asked if there 
were any comments or discussion. 
 
 Mr. Wilson clarified that this resolution reaffirm s actions taken under previous resolutions 
and seeks approval for modifications to the redevelopment plan for the Mohawk Tannery site. 
 
 Attorney Tucker explained that revisions were made  to the project, including an increase 
in the number of units reserved for affordable housing. He noted that these changes will not 
affect the payment amount to the Housing Revolving Trust Fund.  He further stated that the 
project modifications are contingent upon Board of Aldermen redevelopment approval. 
DRAFT
There being no further discussion, the Recording S ecretary called the roll with the 
following responses: 
 
AYE NAY 
James Tollner  
Thomas Monahan  
Helen Honorow  
Paul Deschenes  
Eric Wilson  
 
RESOLUTION NO. 26-2510 
BY THE NASHUA HOUSING AND REDEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY  
AWARDING A TWO-YEAR CONTRACT FOR AUDIT SERVICES  
TO EFPR GROUP, CPAs, PLLC, 6390 MAIN STREET, SUITE 200, WILLIAMSVILLE, NY 
14221 FOR THE FISCAL YEARS ENDING SEPTEMBER 30, 2026 AND SEPTEMBER 30, 
2027 FOR THE NASHUA HOUSING AND REDEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY AND 
NASHUA PARK VIEW APARTMENTS, LLC AT A TOTAL CONTRACT COST OF 
$74,950; $61,620 UNDER THE OPERATING BUDGET AND $13,330 UNDER THE 
NASHUA PARK VIEW APARTMENTS, LLC BUDGET 
 
 The Chairperson entertained a motion to approve Resolution No. 26-2510 . Mr. Monahan 
made a motion, and Ms. Honorow seconded the motion. The Chairperson asked if there were 
any comments or discussion. 
   
 Mr. Wilson asked whether the Authority has used th is company in the past. Ms. Lombardi 
confirmed.  
  
 Mr. Monahan asked whether the Authority is satisfi ed with the company’s services. Ms. 
Lombardi confirmed. 
 
 There being no further discussion, the Recording S ecretary called the roll with the 
following responses: 
 
AYE NAY 
James Tollner  
Thomas Monahan

RESOLUTION NO. 26-2511 
BY THE NASHUA HOUSING AND REDEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY 
AWARDING CONTRACTS FOR INSURANCE COVERAGE FOR  
THE NASHUA HOUSING AND REDEVELOPMENT  AUTHORITY BUSINESS AND 
PROPERTY NEEDS TO HOUSING INSURANCE SERVICES, INC., 189 COMMERCE 
COURT, CHESHIRE, CT 06410 AT A TOTAL CONTRACT COST  
OF $275,016.73 UNDER THE OPERATING BUDGET AND FOR NASHUA PARK VIEW 
APARTMENTS, LLC BUSINESS AND PROPERTY NEEDS AT A TOTAL  
CONTRACT COST OF $11,331.14 UNDER THE NASHUA PARK VIEW  
APARTMENTS, LLC BUDGET 
 
 The Chairperson entertained a motion to approve Resolution No. 26-2511 . Mr. Monahan 
made a motion, and Mr. Tollner seconded the motion.  The Chairperson asked if there were 
any comments or discussion. 
 
 Mr. Wilson noted that the NHRA has been with this provider for a long time. Ms. Lombardi 
confirmed that the NHRA has used this company for m any years and stated that no other 
underwriter has been able to offer a more competitive bid.  
 
 Mr. Monahan acknowledged that twenty-eight invitat ions were mailed to companies. Ms. 
Lombardi explained that HUD waives the requirement to solicit bids when Housing Authority 
Insurance (HAI) is used; however, the NHRA still issues invitations to provide an opportunity 
for lower bids. 
 
 There being no further discussion, the Recording S ecretary called the roll with the 
following responses: 
 
AYE NAY 
James Tollner  
Thomas Monahan  
Helen Honorow  
Paul Deschenes  
Eric Wilson  
DRAFT
RESOLUTION NO. 26-2512 
BY NASHUA HOUSING AND REDEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY 
AUTHORIZING THE FISCAL YEAR 2027 PAYMENT  
STANDARDS EFFECTIVE NOVEMBER 1, 2026 FOR THE SECTION 8  
HOUSING CHOICE VOUCHER PROGRAM (HCV) AS LISTED:  
 
 The Chairperson entertained a motion to approve Resolution No. 26-2512 . Ms. Honorow 
made a motion, and Mr. Deschenes seconded the motio n. The Chairperson asked if there 
were any comments or discussion. 
 
 Mr. Monahan questioned why the NHRA is not utilizi ng the full payment standard of 110%. 
He stated that landlords often look for the highest rent amount offered and expressed interest 
in providing that option. He noted that if landlord s are paid below the maximum allowable 
standard, they may be less inclined to maintain units at a higher level of quality. 
 
 Ms. Lombardi and Mr. Costa explained that, given t he uncertainty of HUD funding, it is 
beneficial to maintain the lower payment standards rather than increasing them. This 
approach provides a reasonable balance between maintaining access to rental housing and 
controlling the program expenditures. Mr. Costa sai d that the NHRA has successfully 
negotiated lower rents with landlords and we will continue to monitor actual leasing outcomes 
and local rent conditions. He noted that Ms. Lombardi can increase payment standards at any 
time, if necessary. 
 
 Mr. Tollner asked whether the NHRA is at risk of l osing any partners by not utilizing the 
full payment standard. Ms. Lombardi confirmed that it is not. 
   
 There being no further discussion, the Recording S ecretary called the roll with the 
following responses: 
 
AYE NAY 
James Tollner  
 Thomas Monahan 
Helen Honorow  
Paul Deschenes  
Eric Wilson  
 
 
DRAFT
RESOLUTION NO. 26-2513 
BY THE NASHUA HOUSING AND REDEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY 
APPROVING THE PUBLIC HOUSING TENANT ACCOUNT RECEIVABLES (TAR)  
WRITE-OFF FOR $75,478.39, AND NASHUA PARK VIEW APARTMENTS, LLC  
TAR WRITE-OFF FOR $551.88 
 
 The Chairperson entertained a motion to approve Resolution No. 26-2513 . Mr. Monahan 
made a motion, and Ms. Honorow seconded the motion. The Chairperson asked if there were 
any comments or discussion. 
 
 Mr. Tollner requested increased communication with  residents to address rent 
receivables. He expressed concern regarding the hig h write-off amount and asked whether 
that amount is associated with unit damage or the bedroom size of the unit. He noted that this 
remains an ongoing issue and should be closely monitored. 
 
 Ms. Lombardi clarified that many of the higher dol lar amounts are a result of many 
circumstances. She explained that some large balances stem from significant damage caused 
to units, and that some cases of non-payment involve residents experiencing drug abuse or 
mental illness. 
 
 Mr. Monahan asked for clarification regarding the eligibility of individuals who owe money 
to a former housing authority. Ms. Lombardi explained that many housing authorities will work 
with individuals who owe money to another housing a gency.  She said if a resident has 
entered a repayment arrangement with the former housing agency and they are not in default 
with their payments, a housing agency may have poli cies enabling them to assist the 
individual. 
 
 Mr. Tollner asked whether there is a way for the N HRA to determine if an individual owes 
money or has an active payment arrangement. Ms. Lom bardi stated that the NHRA uses a 
nationwide database that identifies whether an indi vidual owes money. If a balance is 
indicated, the NHRA contacts the originating housin g authority for additional information, 
including whether a payment arrangement is in place. 
 
 Mr. Wilson sought clarification on whether the wri te-off amounts are included in the rent 
receivables. Ms. Lombardi stated that they are not. 
 
DRAFT
Ms. Honorow asked whether the write-off amounts ar e recorded strictly for accounting 
purposes. Ms. Lombardi confirmed that they are. 
 
 There being no further discussion, the Recording S ecretary called the roll with the 
following responses: 
 
AYE NAY 
James Tollner  
Thomas Monahan  
Helen Honorow  
Paul Deschenes  
Eric Wilson  
 
RESOLUTION NO. 26-2514 
BY THE NASHUA HOUSING AND REDEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY 
APPROVING THE OPERATING BUDGET FOR 
FISCAL YEAR ENDING SEPTEMBER 30, 2027  
 
 The Chairperson entertained a motion to approve Resolution No. 26-2514. Mr. Tollner 
made a motion to table Resolution No. 26-2514, and Mr. Monahan seconded the motion. 
 
 The Chairperson asked if there was any further dis cussion. 
 
 The motion to table Resolution No. 26-2514 passed unanimously. 
 
BILLS/INVESTMENTS: 
 
 The Chairperson called for a motion to pay the bill s as listed on the Cash Disbursement 
List - check numbers 73559 through 73778 and from t he Park View Apartments Cash 
Disbursement List - check numbers 6077 through 6082, including ACH debits and investment 
accounts. Mr. Monahan made a motion, and Mr. Deschenes seconded. 
 
 The Chairperson asked if there were any comments o r discussion. 
 
 Mr. Monahan clarified that the check issued to Nor th Branch Construction was for the 
Phase 1 Maynard Homes Redevelopment project and is reimbursable. 
 
DRAFT
Mr. Tollner inquired about the rent refund check. Ms. Lombardi stated that it was issued 
due to overpayment. 
 
 Mr. Monahan acknowledged that the loan for Park Vi ew was paid off and noted that this 
was very good news. 
 
 There being no further discussion, the motion pass ed unanimously. 
 
COMMISSIONER’S COMMENTS: 
 
 Mr. Tollner elaborated on prior concerns regarding  police patrols at Tyler Street and 
reported that additional patrols will be conducted in the area. He also expanded on an earlier 
comment expressing interest in the NHRA collaborating with similar agencies, such as Harbor 
Care. He further sought clarification regarding Sec tion 8 procedures, specifically, who is 
responsible for inspecting the unit and whether lan dlords are required to notify the NHRA if 
damages occur. Ms. Lombardi explained that that the responsibility of inspecting a unit is that 
of the landlord. She said the NHRA is required to perform NSPIRE inspections on a bi-annual 
basis in all HCV units. Mr. Costa added that if damages occurred in an HCV unit, the landlord 
can and should report the details to the NHRA. 
 
 Mr. Monahan stated that, ultimately, it is the lan dlord’s responsibility to inspect their units 
and report issues to the NHRA related to residents. 
 
 Ms. Honorow expressed appreciation for the photogr aphs showing progress on the 
Maynard Homes Redevelopment project. 
  
ANY OTHER BUSINESS THAT MAY COME BEFORE THE BOARD: 
 
 None. 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT: 
 
 Mr. Mack stated that the rent receivables report may not fully capture the individuals with 
Section 8 whom his agency and other agencies assist . He noted that this assistance is a 
significant financial undertaking and emphasizes to individuals that if they cannot afford their 
thirty percent portion, it will be difficult for th em to afford market rents. He continues to 
encourage residents to establish and maintain payment arrangements. He acknowledged the 
length of the waitlist and said that additional affordable housing is needed. 
DRAFT
Mr. Plodzik shared concerns regarding smoking occu rring within the building. Ms. 
Lombardi and Mr. Tollner requested that he continue to report incidents as they occur. 
  
 Ms. Murphy inquired about the possibility of remov ing or disabling the smoke detectors 
installed in the bedrooms and requested that the ou tdoor benches be painted. She 
commented on the loitering occurring at the benches . Mr. Costa explained that the smoke 
detectors cannot be removed, as they are required b y code for safety. He said that the 
benches would be addressed. 
 
 Ms. Knisley expressed appreciation for the recentl y installed raised garden beds and 
requested that additional beds be added. She also noted that Rivier University volunteers are 
interested in assisting residents who have difficulty performing daily tasks. Additionally, she 
mentioned uncertainty as to whether the NHRA would permit a company she is collaborating 
with to install window insulation in units to help prevent winter drafts. 
 
NONPUBLIC SESSION: 
 
 The Chairperson entertained a motion to enter nonp ublic session. Mr. Tollner moved to 
enter nonpublic session, and Ms. Honorow seconded.  
 
 The Chairperson asked if there were any comments o r discussion.  He said the purpose 
of the meeting is to address confidential personnel matters. 
 
 There being no further discussion, the Executive D irector called the roll with the following 
responses: 
    
AYE NAY 
James Tollner  
Thomas Monahan  
Helen Honorow  
Paul Deschenes  
Eric Wilson  
 
 The Board entered nonpublic session at approximately 10:06 a.m. 
 
DRAFT
The Chairperson entertained a motion to rise from nonpublic session and resume the regular 
meeting.  Ms. Honorow made a motion, and Mr. Tollner seconded the motion. 
 
 The Chairperson asked if there were any comments o r discussion. 
 
 The Chairperson entertained a motion to approve Resolution No. 26-2514  and the salary 
recommendations . Mr. Tollner made a motion, and Ms. Honorow seconded the motion. 
 
 There being no further discussion, the Executive D irector called the roll with the following 
responses: 
   
AYE NAY 
James Tollner  
Thomas Monahan  
Helen Honorow  
Paul Deschenes  
Eric Wilson  
 
 The Board rose from nonpublic session and resumed the regular meeting at approximately 
10:19 a.m. 
 
ADJOURNMENT: 
 
 The Chairperson entertained a motion to adjourn. M r. Wilson moved to adjourn, and Ms. 
Honorow seconded the motion.  
 
 There being no further discussion, the motion pass ed unanimously.  
 
 The meeting adjourned at approximately 10:19 a.m. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
 
Deanna Brooks 
Recording Secretary
